brief.scope: the fix round on lane/effort-per-role-2 since your first audit (record 20260903T232447Z-review-codex-9c696a on 03cf55c): commit 024f220 'dispatch: enforce effort and read-role policy' and the seven test commits before it. Aim at: does the job-name guard in ops/conductor/tools/dispatch.sh close the indirect-expansion path you reproduced, and does it open another; is a Codex read role now confined and a read-role snapshot change now invalidating; does the record validator compare exact effort tokens against harness.argv. Everything else in the diff was audited before.

findings.claim: Codex confinement is not bound on resume. Passing read-only or danger-full-access produces identical argv with no sandbox token, while the record continues to advertise its prior sandbox. The resumed process therefore relies on unchecked vendor session/default state rather than the recorded policy.
findings.reproduce:
PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 - <<'PY'
import sys
from pathlib import Path
sys.path.insert(0,'ops/devlane/dispatch')
import launch
args=('codex','M','xhigh','00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000',Path('/tmp/job/prompt.txt'),[])
a=launch._argv(*args,'read-only',resume=True)
b=launch._argv(*args,'danger-full-access',resume=True)
print({'identical':a==b,'argv':a})
assert a==b and '--sandbox' not in a
PY

findings.claim: A resumed read job bypasses the new snapshot-integrity enforcement. _resume runs the harness and writes the record directly, never calling _settle, which is the sole location checking read-role HEAD and residual changes.
findings.reproduce:
python3 - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
s=Path('ops/devlane/dispatch/launch.py').read_text()
b=s.split('def _resume(args):',1)[1].split('def _close(args):',1)[0]
assert '_run_attempt(' in b and '_write_record(' in b and '_settle(' not in b
assert s.count('read-role-snapshot: snapshot must be unchanged')==1
print('resume bypasses sole read-role snapshot guard')
PY

findings.claim: Fresh read-job integrity checks omit Git-ignored paths. A policy-only read harness can create or alter ignored local configuration or secret files such as .env.local without residual_paths becoming non-empty, so an approving envelope is not invalidated.
findings.reproduce:
python3 - <<'PY'
import subprocess
from pathlib import Path
s=Path('ops/devlane/dispatch/launch.py').read_text()
b=s.split('def _residual(snapshot):',1)[1].split('def _settle',1)[0]
ignored=subprocess.check_output(['git','check-ignore','-v','--no-index','.env.local','.claude/settings.local.json','config/secrets/prod/prod.decrypt.private.php'],text=True).splitlines()
print({'uses_ignored': '--ignored' in b, 'ignored': ignored})
assert '--ignored' not in b and len(ignored)==3
PY

findings.claim: The effort validator compares harness.argv with a self-declared subsequence, not the canonical adapter carrier. effort_argv=['xhigh'] validates when xhigh appears only as a model value, so a record can claim xhigh although no effort option reached the CLI.
findings.reproduce: cd ops/devlane/dispatch/tests && PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -c 'from test_record import _RecordCase; c=_RecordCase("runTest"); r=c.built(); r["model"]["effort_requested"]="xhigh"; r["model"]["effort_argv"]=["xhigh"]; r["harness"]["argv"]=["grok","--model","xhigh","--output-format","plain"]; v=c.recmod().validate(r); print(v["model"]["effort_argv"],v["harness"]["argv"])'

findings.claim: The job-name guard closes the command-substitution path but reflects the rejected value unescaped into the one-line refusal log. A newline-bearing job name injects additional forged stderr records.
findings.reproduce:
python3 - <<'PY'
import subprocess
j='x\nclass: forged; found trusted; needed none'
p=subprocess.run(['bash','ops/conductor/tools/dispatch.sh','--job',j,'--harness','codex','--scope-file','ops/README.md','--worktree','.','--dry-run'],capture_output=True,text=True)
print({'returncode':p.returncode,'stderr_lines':p.stderr.splitlines()})
assert p.returncode==3 and len(p.stderr.splitlines())==2
PY

envelope.note: Read all 3,085 diff lines (SHA-256 b29f064653a0a86ee48f50e0ec68bb0456990eac0f689df0ffe2d19c387d1dec), required contracts, lane instructions, and the prior audit; in/ was present and empty. The original indirect-expansion exploit is closed, and fresh Codex reads receive --sandbox read-only without writable roots. Secret scan was clean across 28 changed tracked files; no SQL, Twig, dependency, lockfile, fetched-action, or permission-mode changes were found beyond those reported. Live vendor execution, network behavior, and destructive containment probes were not covered. Tempdir-backed integration tests could not start in this read-only environment; the eight non-temp effort-record tests passed. The tree remained clean.
